chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Sa'd ibn Isma'il from his father who said:

I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him) about the guardian of orphans when the orphans reach maturity, and he presents to them what belongs to them, but they refuse to accept it from him. What should he do? He said: 'He returns it to them and compels them to accept it.'
ai.seo_question: What should a guardian do if adult orphans refuse to accept their inheritance?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS), the concept of 'ikrah' (compulsion) is applied specifically to the acceptance of property rights, distinguishing it from general legal compulsion. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that while orphans may refuse the burden of guardianship or management, they cannot permanently forfeit their inherent ownership rights, thus the guardian must enforce the transfer to finalize their legal status as owners.
